Tyrosine hydroxylase forms L-DOPA in the cytosol; aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase forms dopamine. VMAT2 can transport dopamine into secretory vesicles. In cells expressing dopamine beta-hydroxylase, dopamine is converted to noradrenaline inside those vesicles, using copper and ascorbate. In cells expressing PNMT, noradrenaline returns to the cytosol for SAM-dependent conversion to adrenaline, which can be repackaged. These are cell-specific branches, not a compulsory chain in every dopamine neuron. Dopamine is the same molecule in peripheral and brain compartments.

Read the diagram explanation and sources

ATP hydrolysis powers the vesicular proton pump, V-ATPase, which acidifies the vesicle. VMAT2 exchanges vesicular protons for cytosolic monoamines such as dopamine. It therefore uses an existing proton gradient rather than directly hydrolysing ATP itself. Stored transmitter can subsequently be released by exocytosis. This explains a normal mechanism, not evidence of a VMAT2 defect in a particular reader.

The site's throughline is that ADHD is best understood at the level of

. Think of a motherboard rather than a single clock. One weak component can limit a system that looks fine elsewhere, and different people can have different weak components. The model draws on established biochemistry (flux through a pathway is limited by its slowest steps). As an account of ADHD it is
: a hypothesis that predicts that different people will have different bottlenecks, and that has not been tested person-by-person.
What this evidence can tell us
The table is a teaching model. Real dopamine signalling has feedback loops, and the same symptom can come from different steps.
A gene in the table is not an ADHD gene unless the ADHD column says so, and even then only at the stated tier.
Single-gene conditions in the table are rare and mostly present in childhood. They are included because they show which steps are clinically important, not because they explain typical ADHD.
No claim here is about any individual's biology.
